status: parameterised engine with calibration; every default is replaceable by a logged-bake calibration

progress_integration.equation: P = sum over phases of dt / tau(T_dough(t), inputs); the endpoint is reached when P = 1
progress_integration.sourdough_equivalent: G = integral of mu(T_dough(t)) dt; rise R = iota (exp(G) - 1); endpoint when G = ln(K / iota)
progress_integration.time_step: integrate T_dough(t) in steps of 5 min or less during cooling and warming, 15 min otherwise
progress_integration.dough_temperature: use a probe reading when the user gives one; otherwise the Newton model in 'cooling_warming'
progress_integration.phase_carry_over: P (or G) carries over between bulk, bench, shaped proof and fridge; shaping does not reset it
progress_integration.note: additivity of rate over a temperature history is the standard assumption of predictive microbiology; it ignores adaptation lag after a temperature step, which matters most on warm-up from the fridge

endpoints.definition: fractional volume rise R of an aliquot taken right after mixing, straight-sided jar, same temperature as the dough

sourdough.mapping: K = R + iota  (tau = ln(K / iota) / mu)

yeast.basis: at a bakery dose the gas production stays roughly constant over three hours (58.5, 65.5 and 57.5 mL/g measured after 60, 120 and 180 min at 30 C with 3 % yeast, Codina 2013 Table 2), which gives a near-linear rise after a short lag (+50 % at 0.60 of the doubling time); a dough that still grows its yeast rises like a sourdough (+50 % at about 0.79); the engine takes the midpoint. personal_calibration.parameter: v multiplies the rate (mu_ref for sourdough and starters, 1 / tau for yeast); one v per culture, optionally one per recipe family

s0_sourdough.from: sd of ln v across 6 sources = 0.362 (v from 0.51 to 1.59)

s0_yeast.from: sd of ln(observed / engine) inside groups of independent tables and recipes, 0.35-0.56

personal_calibration.observation: y = ln(engine hours at v = 1 over the logged temperature history / observed hours to the logged endpoint) = ln v + e

se.note: tabulated sources scatter by 0.10; home logs add endpoint and thermometer error

personal_calibration.update: precision = 1 / s0^2 + n / se^2; mean = (sum(y) / se^2) / precision; v = exp(mean)

replay.source: Wraith table, 2 % salt, doubling (true v about 1.6)

personal_calibration.anchor: store the mean dough temperature of the logged bakes (T_anchor); the band widens with distance from it

uncertainty.sd: sd^2 = sd_v^2 + se^2 + (s_T * min(|T - T_anchor|, 10))^2 + sum(modifier terms^2) + sum(domain penalties^2)

terms.sd_v: posterior sd of ln v (prior: 0.35 sourdough, 0.45 yeast)

s_T_per_C.from: half the gap between the engine's temperature slope and the flatter slopes of independent data (sourdough 0.122 vs 0.071 per C at 19-23 C; yeast 0.137 vs 0.074 per C at 18-30 C)

terms.modifier: ln(range high / range low) / 2.56 for each modifier that differs from 1
terms.domain_penalty_relief: halve a penalty once at least two logged bakes lie in that same domain

uncertainty.extrapolation_flag: set whenever a domain penalty applies, a modifier with confidence 'low' differs from 1, or P is integrated mostly outside 10-30 C

failure_regions.region: sourdough below 10 C and any retard
failure_regions.why: the temperature curve is a broth growth model that its authors call poor near Tmin; the alternative model puts the yeast's Tmin at 8 C. One practitioner estimate (24 h at 3 C is worth at most 30 min of warm bulk) agrees with the engine (32 min)
failure_regions.behaviour: predict, flag, widen (penalty 0.40); express fridge time as equivalent hours at 25 C

failure_regions.why: yeast and lactobacilli part ways (optima 27 and 32-33 C): acidity outruns gas; proteolysis can ruin the dough before the rise target
failure_regions.behaviour: predict, flag, widen; advise a lower rise target

failure_regions.region: sourdough past the endpoint (iota exp(G) above about 1.5)
failure_regions.why: acid stall and gluten breakdown; the exponential rise law no longer holds
failure_regions.behaviour: report 'over-fermented by x h equivalent', do not report a rise

failure_regions.why: Wraith adds a gluten penalty above 15 %; below 0.5 % no data

failure_regions.region: starter not at peak, or of unknown age
yeast direct doughs at bakery doses (0.4 % IDY and more) judged at +50 %
failure_regions.why: recipe schedules run 1.2-1.6 times the engine; a private log (aggregate only, n = 2, temperatures not probe-measured) ran slower still
failure_regions.behaviour: report the upper half of the band as the likely side; calibrate on the first bake

failure_regions.region: rich dough (sugar above 10 %, fat above 30 %) or a preferment dosed far above the validated range, in the fridge
failure_regions.why: private observations (aggregate only) showed far less visible rise than predicted; cold fat stiffens the dough and the modifiers were not measured cold
failure_regions.behaviour: flag; do not promise a visible rise in the fridge

failure_regions.region: yeast doses above 1 % IDY or predictions under 45 min
failure_regions.why: chart floored at 2 h; adaptation lag not in the power law

failure_regions.region: yeast between 18 and 30 C far from the calibration temperature
failure_regions.why: the chart's temperature slope (Q10 3.4-3.9) is steeper than rules of thumb and compiled tables (Q10 about 2.1)
failure_regions.behaviour: s_T term; calibrate at the temperature actually used

failure_regions.why: chart rows were tuned to schedules that include cooling and warm-up; published cold schedules scatter by a factor 2.2

failure_regions.region: sweet and rich doughs (sugar above 10 %, fat above 20 %), spices, cocoa
failure_regions.why: modifiers are manufacturer curves or reasoned ranges, not dough-time measurements
failure_regions.behaviour: flag, widen, offer a recipe-specific calibration

failure_regions.why: rise targets and gas retention differ; no data fitted
